findings.title: Team admin/owner check requires both roles simultaneously
findings.body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed with `&&` between `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner`, so a user must be both admin and owner to pass. A team admin who is not owner, or an owner who is not admin, is denied. The intent is clearly `||`. Also, when teamId is 0 (no team), both helpers are called with 0 unnecessarily.

findings.title: Email sent with raw input guests instead of actually-added guests
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the original input list, but `uniqueGuests` (after filtering existing attendees and blacklisted emails) is what was actually persisted. Existing attendees who were re-submitted, or blacklisted emails, are treated as 'new guests' and get the scheduled-event email, and the newly added attendees are not correctly classified.

findings.title: Email failure silently swallowed with no error detail
findings.body: The try/catch around `sendAddGuestsEmails` logs a fixed string and drops the error object, so failures are hard to diagnose. The handler still returns success even when notifications failed, which is inconsistent with the rest of the flow.

findings.title: Calendar update runs after DB write with no rollback and uses unfiltered booking
findings.body: Attendees are written to the DB (line 92) before `updateCalendarAttendees` is called. If the calendar update throws, the guests are persisted but the calendar invite is never sent, leaving inconsistent state. The `booking` object passed to updateCalendarAttendees is the pre-update snapshot, so the new attendees may not be reflected there.

findings.title: Guests created with empty name
findings.body: Each new guest is created with `name: ""`, so downstream emails and the attendee list show a blank name and the email template uses `attendee.name` in greetings and calendar invites.

findings.title: Subject line uses first attendee name instead of the guest/organizer
findings.body: In OrganizerAddGuestsEmail the subject uses `this.calEvent.attendees[0].name`, which may be the booker, not a meaningful identifier, and can be an empty string for newly added guests if they are ordered first. This makes subjects inconsistent.

findings.title: Organizer email replyTo includes all attendees and is sent to organizer
findings.body: `replyTo` lists the organizer and every attendee, and the `to` address is only the organizer or team member. Replies from the organizer's client will fan out to all guests, which may be unintended and leaks guest addresses in the reply chain.

findings.title: Templates exported from index but used via different naming
findings.body: The new React templates are exported from the index, but the mail templates import `renderEmail("AttendeeAddGuestsEmail")`/`OrganizerAddGuestsEmail` by name. The naming pattern diverges from neighboring templates and is easy to mismatch when adding or renaming templates.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails never awaits or returns the reminder promise in related path and lacks team-member handling for attendees
findings.body: The new function sends scheduled emails to existing attendees via AttendeeScheduledEmail for new guests, but `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` compares raw input emails case-sensitively against stored attendee emails, so mismatched casing sends the wrong template to the wrong recipient.

findings.title: Keys by index cause input state mismatch on removal
findings.body: Rows use `key={index}`, so removing an email in the middle shifts the remaining inputs. Since the component is controlled via value array, this can cause focus/caret glitches and wrong value display during edits.

findings.title: Hardcoded English tooltip text
findings.body: The tooltip content "Remove email" is not wrapped in `t()`, unlike all other user-facing strings in the component, breaking localization.

findings.title: Zod schema recreated each render and duplicate check ignores empty entries
findings.body: The schema is redefined inside the component on every render. Additionally, the initial state `[""]` contains an empty string, so `z.string().email()` fails and the user sees an error only after clicking Add; the dialog gives no guidance on which entry is invalid.

findings.title: Error toast message concatenates code with translated message
findings.body: `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}` produces messages like "BAD_REQUEST: emails_must_be_unique_valid" when `t` lacks the key, and `message || t(...)` fallback is dead code because the template string is never empty. The toast shows raw error codes to users.

findings.title: Cancel/close does not reset invalid-email state on dialog dismiss
findings.body: `onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}` closes the dialog without resetting `multiEmailValue` or `isInvalidEmail`, so reopening shows stale input and error state, unlike the Cancel button which resets them.

findings.title: Organizer lookup uses booking.userId and fails for orphaned bookings
findings.body: `findFirstOrThrow` on `booking.userId || 0` throws a Prisma NotFound error (not a TRPCError) when the booking has no organizer, producing an unhandled 500 instead of a clean error.
